overview: Wires F-2's three typed discovery states (ToolMissing, NoDeviceFound, PollFailed) and the multi-device case into the already-shipped ErrorCard/CommandBlock/SourceListRow components (FR-23), adds the non-blocking stream-drop banner over a stale mirror (FR-24), and fixes a real regression: F-4's merged session-loss path routes through resumeLive and clears staged annotations plus the frozen frame, violating NFR-6's 'survive a full disconnect/reconnect cycle' requirement. Three of four acceptance criteria are pure wiring against fully-formed kit components; the fourth (NFR-6) is a behavioural fix to shipped code, and the only test written against it must first be demonstrated failing — the area has already produced one vacuous session-loss test that passed against deleted code.
problemStatement: F-2 deliberately left ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound/PollFailed unrendered and F-4 shipped a session-loss path that clears annotations on any disconnect by reusing the user-initiated Resume Live code path. Neither gap is cosmetic: an unrendered error state means a tester sees nothing actionable when adb is missing or no device is found, and annotation loss on a stream drop destroys unsent bug reports the moment a USB cable wiggles.
purpose: Make every recoverable failure mode (missing tool, no device, multiple devices, mid-session disconnect) produce a clear, actionable, keyboard-navigable card or banner, and guarantee that an involuntary disconnect never discards work the way a deliberate Resume Live click intentionally does.
goals: Wire, not author: ErrorCard/CommandBlock/SourceListRow already have the exact shape FR-23 needs; zero new atoms/molecules.
Fix NFR-6 at the root: separate the involuntary-disconnect path from resumeLive's deliberate clear-and-return-to-live semantics so a session loss can never take the clearing branch.
Prove the NFR-6 fix with a test that is shown failing against the pre-fix code first — this exact area already shipped one test that passed against deleted code.
Resolve PollFailed explicitly rather than silently folding it into NoDeviceFound, since F-2's own KDoc says the two assert different things.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given adb is not found on PATH (DiscoveryModel.ToolMissing), then an ErrorCard renders with the platform install command in a copyable CommandBlock, primary action 'Locate adb…', secondary action 'Retry', and a footer line listing the probed paths and $ANDROID_HOME state.

Given no Android device is detected after repeated polls (DiscoveryModel.NoDeviceFound), then an ErrorCard renders with the kill-server command, primary action 'Restart adb', secondary action 'Boot emulator instead', and a footer line showing tool version, last-poll age, and attached count.

Given 3 devices are connected simultaneously, then an ErrorCard renders an inline SourceListRow list of all attached devices (not a modal), every row enabled and clickable to mirror that device directly, with the card's primary action labeled 'Mirror <top device>' as a one-click shortcut to the first-listed device.

Given a stream drops mid-session with staged annotations present, then a non-blocking banner appears over the stale (frozen) mirror reading 'Stream dropped' / 'Your N annotations are kept on the frozen frame', with a primary 'Reconnect' action; 'Resolve & Send' remains clickable and every staged annotation remains pinned and unchanged while disconnected.

Given adb itself fails or times out mid-poll (DiscoveryModel.PollFailed), then an ErrorCard renders distinct from the NoDeviceFound card — title/body convey a tool-level failure (not an empty device bench), footer shows the tool name and failure reason, primary action 'Retry'.

Given staged annotations and a frozen frame exist, when the session is lost involuntarily (onSessionLost, not a user-initiated Resume Live click) and later reconnects, then every staged annotation and the frozen frame are bit-for-bit unchanged before and after the cycle; this test is run against the pre-fix code first and demonstrated to fail (annotations/frame cleared) before the fix lands, per this chain's prior vacuous-test incident.
Given any ErrorCard instance (AC-26/27/28/53) or the stream-drop banner (AC-29), then every primary/secondary/copy/row action is reachable via Tab and activatable via Enter/Space without a pointer.

Given the light and dark themes, then ErrorCard (all four states) and the stream-drop banner meet the project's existing contrast baseline (same method as presentation-core-styling's PaletteContrastTest), with no state relying on a signal color that differs between themes.

functionalRequirements.text: Render ErrorCard instances for DiscoveryModel's typed discovery-failure states: ToolMissing (FR-23a / AC-26), NoDeviceFound (FR-23b / AC-27), and multiple-devices-connected (FR-23c / AC-28) — wiring only, zero new kit primitives. NOTE: this id collides with an unrelated FR-23 already minted by app-shell-window-layout's clarify.json ('signal colors render identically in light/dark'); this spec's FR-23 is the PRD-canonical id for the structured error card and takes precedence per the approved PRD — see traceNotes.

On a mid-session stream drop, show a non-blocking floating banner over the stale (frozen) mirror: 'Stream dropped' / 'Your N annotations are kept on the frozen frame', primary action 'Reconnect'; staged annotations stay pinned and 'Resolve & Send' remains usable while disconnected. NOTE: this id collides with an unrelated FR-24 already minted by android-device-discovery-mirroring's clarify.json ('v1 screenshot-polling mirror transport'); this spec's FR-24 is the PRD-canonical id for the stream-drop banner and takes precedence per the approved PRD — see traceNotes.

Render DiscoveryModel.PollFailed as its own ErrorCard state, distinct from NoDeviceFound — its KDoc explicitly distinguishes 'nothing learned' (poll itself failed/timed out) from 'nothing attached' (bench confirmed empty). Title/body/footer convey the tool-level failure and its reason string; primary action 'Retry'.

Split F-4's session-termination handling into two distinct code paths: involuntary disconnect (onSessionLost) must not invoke resumeLive's clear-annotations/clear-frozen-frame logic. Instead it transitions to a 'disconnected, frame and annotations preserved' sub-state that FR-24's banner renders over. The user-initiated Resume Live control (F-4's AC-51) keeps its existing clear-and-return-to-live behavior unchanged — the two are different user intents and must not share a code path.

The multiple-devices-connected card's inline device list uses SourceListRow with every row enabled (F-2's enabled parameter) and clickable to mirror that device directly; the card's primary action is a convenience shortcut equivalent to clicking the top-listed row, not a separate flow.

The stream-drop banner's 'Reconnect' action re-attempts the capture/transport session against the same sessionDeviceId; on success the stage returns to live, the banner dismisses, and all staged annotations remain intact; on repeated failure the banner persists rather than silently disappearing.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Stream-drop handling must preserve all staged annotations and the frozen frame without loss across a disconnect/reconnect cycle. CURRENTLY VIOLATED by merged F-4 code: onSessionLost's downstream path reaches resumeLive's clear logic. This spec's FR-33 is the fix.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers, Tab/Enter for error-card and banner actions).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.

outOfScope: Measurement/measure-mode (F-5), payload preview (F-6), MCP send (F-7), capture/annotation history (F-8), iOS (F-10).
Closing SEC-1 (F-2's unvalidated GetProp free text into adb shell) — stays open; this spec must not become GetProp's first production caller without closing it first.
New visual primitives — every element is assembled from ErrorCard/CommandBlock/SourceListRow/AppButton/StatusIndicator/DeviceChip, already shipped.
Design comps for AC-28 and FR-24 — none exist; both are derived from shipped components with invented values recorded as named constants, not pixel-measured against a comp.

constraints.text: No literal Color(0x...), raw .dp, or hardcoded TextStyle at any new call site; invented values (banner geometry, reconnect-retry delay) are named constants or Theme tokens.
commonTest names: plain camelCase only — a backtick name with a comma/apostrophe/colon compiles on the JVM but fails compileTestKotlinIosArm64 (already broke the repo build once, per F-1).
withTimeoutOrNull only, never withTimeout, for any reconnect-retry logic — resultLauncher's existing CancellationException handling depends on this.
Every new user-facing string gets an actually-referenced mirror_*-style localisation key; no dead keys (F-4's T-12 precedent).
Keep the existing 196 desktop tests green; this spec adds tests, it does not destabilize the suite.
NFR-6's test must be shown failing against pre-fix code before the fix lands and the suite is declared green — a test that cannot fail is worse than no test (this chain has shipped one already).

assumptions.text: PollFailed gets its own distinct ErrorCard state rather than folding into NoDeviceFound (per survey Q1/FR-32).
F-4's resumeLive (user-initiated Resume Live button, AC-51) keeps clearing annotations/frame unchanged; only the involuntary onSessionLost path is rerouted away from it (per survey Q2/FR-33).

AC-28's device list rows are individually clickable/enabled to mirror that device directly, with the primary button as a convenience shortcut to the top row, not a separate confirm step (per survey Q3/FR-34).
The banner's 'N annotations' count reads the same staged-annotation list F-4 already exposes to the toolbar's CounterBadge/stagedCounter slot — no new counting logic.

dependencies.note: DiscoveryModel's ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound/PollFailed typed states; SourceListRow's enabled parameter for AC-28.

MirrorViewModel.onSessionLost/resumeLive, the Orbit staged-annotation state, and the separate frozen-bitmap StateFlow that FR-33 must stop routing through resumeLive's clear path on involuntary disconnect.
ErrorCard, CommandBlock, SourceListRow, AppButton, StatusIndicator, DeviceChip — all reused as-is.

scenarios.title: adb not on PATH shows install-command error card
steps: Launch with adb missing from PATH
ErrorCard renders with copyable install command
Footer shows probed paths and $ANDROID_HOME state
Click Retry re-probes

scenarios.title: No device detected shows kill-server error card
steps: Launch with no device attached after repeated polls
ErrorCard renders with kill-server command
Footer shows tool version/last-poll/attached count
Click 'Boot emulator instead'

scenarios.title: Multiple devices connected shows inline list, not a modal
steps: Connect 3 devices simultaneously
ErrorCard renders inline SourceListRow list, all enabled
Click a non-top row to mirror that device directly
Click primary action to mirror the top device as a shortcut

scenarios.title: Stream drop preserves annotations and keeps Resolve & Send usable
steps: Stage annotations on a frozen frame
Drop the stream mid-session (involuntary disconnect)
Non-blocking banner appears; annotations remain pinned, unchanged
Click 'Resolve & Send' while still disconnected — remains clickable
Click Reconnect; stage returns to live with annotations intact

scenarios.title: PollFailed renders distinctly from NoDeviceFound
steps: Force adb to time out mid-poll (PollFailed)
Assert the rendered card differs from the NoDeviceFound card
Footer shows tool name and failure reason, not attached-count stats

scenarios.title: NFR-6 regression test demonstrated failing before the fix
steps: Run the disconnect/reconnect annotation-survival test against pre-fix (merged) code
Confirm it fails (annotations/frame cleared via resumeLive)
Apply FR-33's path split
Re-run; confirm it now passes

successMetrics: 196 pre-existing desktop tests stay green; new tests added for AC-26/27/28/29/53/54/55.
AC-54's NFR-6 regression test is documented as failing against pre-fix code, then passing after FR-33 lands — closing this chain's second vacuous-test risk.
openQuestions: Exact retry/backoff cadence for the banner's Reconnect action beyond 'persist on repeated failure' is left to implementation; no SLA was specified upstream.
SEC-1 (F-2's unvalidated GetProp) remains open; revisit only if a later spec needs device properties.

Exact copy for PollFailed's title/body is not specified upstream (no design comp); implementation should pick plain language distinguishing 'adb itself failed' from 'no device found' and record the string as a named mirror_* key.

The PRD's canonical ids are kept here per the aggregate's explicit instruction; Stage 5 must treat SC-10/SC-11 as spec-scoped, not globally unique.

proposedSurvey.question: DiscoveryModel.PollFailed (tool itself failed/timed out) is KDoc'd as distinct from NoDeviceFound (bench confirmed empty), but no AC names it and no comp illustrates it. Should F-3 render it as its own ErrorCard state?
options: A) Give PollFailed its own ErrorCard state distinct from NoDeviceFound — title/body convey a tool-level failure, footer shows the reason string, primary 'Retry' (FR-32/AC-53/SC-14).
B) Fold PollFailed into the NoDeviceFound card's rendering, ignoring the KDoc's stated distinction.
C) Render nothing special for PollFailed (silent auto-retry, no card).
proposedSurvey.recommended: A) Give PollFailed its own ErrorCard state distinct from NoDeviceFound — title/body convey a tool-level failure, footer shows the reason string, primary 'Retry' (FR-32/AC-53/SC-14).
proposedSurvey.rationale: F-2's own KDoc explicitly says these are not the same assertion ('nothing learned' vs 'nothing attached'); a tester who sees 'No Android device detected' when adb itself crashed gets actionable-looking advice (check USB cabling) for the wrong problem. ErrorCard already supports this with zero new primitives — the cost of option A is one more typed-state branch, not new UI. Option B contradicts the codebase's own documented semantics; option C leaves the user with no information on an actual tool failure, which is worse than any ambiguity it resolves.

proposedSurvey.question: NFR-6 is violated because F-4's onSessionLost reaches resumeLive's clear-annotations/clear-frame logic. How should the fix be structured relative to AC-51 (F-4's user-initiated Resume Live, which is SUPPOSED to clear annotations)?
options: A) Split into two distinct paths: involuntary disconnect (onSessionLost) never calls resumeLive's clear logic at all — it moves to a separate 'disconnected, preserved' sub-state; the user-initiated Resume Live button keeps its existing clear-and-return behavior completely unchanged (FR-33).
B) Change resumeLive itself to stop clearing annotations/frame, affecting both the disconnect path and the user-initiated button — meaning AC-51 (Resume Live clears the staged list) no longer holds.
C) Parameterize the shared function (e.g. resumeLive(preserve: Boolean)) called with different values from the two call sites, keeping one function for both intents.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A) Split into two distinct paths: involuntary disconnect (onSessionLost) never calls resumeLive's clear logic at all — it moves to a separate 'disconnected, preserved' sub-state; the user-initiated Resume Live button keeps its existing clear-and-return behavior completely unchanged (FR-33).
proposedSurvey.rationale: AC-51 (F-4, already shipped and confirmed) explicitly requires Resume Live to clear the staged list — that is a deliberate, confirmed user intent ('I'm done with this frame, discard it'), not a bug. Option B would silently break a confirmed acceptance criterion from a merged spec. Option C keeps one function serving two unrelated intents behind a boolean flag, which is exactly the kind of shared-code-path smell that caused this bug in the first place — a disconnect accidentally routing through logic meant only for a deliberate discard. Option A is the smallest change that makes the two intents structurally impossible to conflate again.

proposedSurvey.question: AC-28's PRD text says 'inline device list rather than a modal, primary action naming the top device' but doesn't specify whether non-top rows are independently actionable. How should the list and the primary action compose?
options: A) Every row is enabled and clickable to mirror that specific device directly (reusing F-2's existing SourceListRow.enabled); the card's primary action is a one-click shortcut equivalent to clicking the top row — no separate confirm step, no modal (FR-34).
B) Rows are display-only (disabled/non-interactive); a secondary action 'Choose device…' reopens F-2's existing picker modal for selection.
C) Drop ErrorCard for this case entirely and reuse F-2's device-picker panel directly, pre-filtered to attached devices only.
proposedSurvey.recommended: A) Every row is enabled and clickable to mirror that specific device directly (reusing F-2's existing SourceListRow.enabled); the card's primary action is a one-click shortcut equivalent to clicking the top row — no separate confirm step, no modal (FR-34).
proposedSurvey.rationale: The PRD text explicitly says 'inline device list rather than a modal' — option B's secondary action reopening a modal, and option C's full modal reuse, both reintroduce the exact interaction the PRD says to avoid. F-2 already built SourceListRow's enabled parameter for exactly this kind of clickable-row scenario (A11Y-6: disabled means no handler AND marked disabled, which is the inverse of what's needed here — enabled rows with real click handlers). Making the primary button a shortcut to the top row, rather than a separate flow, keeps the component honest: the button does exactly what clicking the top row would do.
